verdict.rationale: Galileo can be driven without its UI. A Python SDK checks application performance in code, a published OpenAPI 3.1 REST API (202 /v2 paths) authenticates with a real token, and experiments can be run outside the console. That supports headless automation, but nothing in the pack documents CI use specifically. Missing for 10: a documented CI/CD integration or guide (e.g., running experiments as a pipeline gate), a CLI, and independent or hands-on corroboration of headless/CI runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: Galileo publishes a downloadable OpenAPI 3.1.0 document at its API origin (202 paths, all under /v2/)
executes against the production API with a real token
Thanks to Galileo's Python SDK we'll be able to check the application's performance and tool selection.
Experiments allow you to evaluate prompts, models, and your application code, using well-defined inputs, against metrics of your choice.
